gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-brawler: Aaargh draws every curve and stem with one uniform, tube-like line, which gives it a blunt, commanding presence at the top. Brawler adds a gentle thick-thin rhythm.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-brygada-1918: Aaargh hits hard with its commanding, uniform line, curves and straights alike. Brygada 1918 brings the mild swelling of a worn felt marker, a traditional, dignified voice for the paragraphs.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-cinzel: Classic and editorial, Cinzel is spaced loosely below a tube-like heading. Aaargh stays constant in width while Cinzel's joins taper modestly, so the two keep a steady, orderly conversation going down the page.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-inria-serif: Dignified is the first word for this pairing, with Aaargh looping its strokes like bent plastic tubing. Inria Serif answers with wide-mouthed round letters and slightly lighter diagonals, which makes the difference between them the main attraction.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-joan: Aaargh looks sketched with a pencil that never presses harder. Joan follows beneath with gentle weight shifts and slightly thinner joins, giving the heading's flat line something softer to lean against.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-junge: Authoritative from the first line, Aaargh holds its strokes straight-edged and constant. Junge keeps its curve gaps generous and thins its bowls gracefully, so a longer passage reads with a steady, dignified pace.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-libertinus-serif: Aaargh sets down lines with the weight of a technical drawing pen, and that bluntness is what it does best. And Libertinus Serif is at its best in curves whose thinnest points still carry real weight.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-maitree: Blunt up top, graceful below. Aaargh has no thin hairline anywhere, while Maitree makes a measured swell from hairline to stem, and that pen-like difference is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-marcellus: Neon-tube letters glow at the top, one steady thickness all the way round, with Marcellus beneath like lines etched in glass. Shrink Aaargh and it loses its glow; enlarge Marcellus and its subtle weight change starts to show.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-poly: Poly is the bookish one here, with bowls that thin slightly at the sides and terminals pulled back from the curve. Poly's mild, approachable contrast sits easily under Aaargh, whose plain constant-width lines hold the top.
